model: Codex editorial application of specific review findings

passages.text: Nevertheless, all of you should recognize that the bishop toils more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, preside as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Accordingly, in your undertaking to administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will give you in return the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through just administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
lexical_decisions.chosen: the bishop toils more than all of you
lexical_decisions.rationale: γινώσκετε takes the accusative τὸν ἐπίσκοπον with its supplementary or predicative participle κάμνοντα. The phrase compares the bishop’s wearisome labor with that of the hearers; this is not an accusative–infinitive construction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου
lexical_decisions.chosen: each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between each member’s individual distress and the bishop’s additional burden for every member.
Combines Clement’s leading position with the explicitly stated role of helping those under his care.

lexical_decisions.chosen: burdened with the cares of everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive participle portrays Clement as loaded with the collective concerns of the community.

Treats σέ as the accusative subject of the whole infinitival expression: Clement undertakes the administration just assigned to him. This accords with the immediate commission and does not force σέ to be the object of οἰκονομεῖν.
The adjective describes a reward that cannot be removed or taken away.
Preserves the expression’s image of righteousness reaching its furthest extent.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον
lexical_decisions.chosen: to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hunting image of θηρεύω, the advantageous character of the praise, and Χριστός as an independent title.

source_issues.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
source_issues.issue: The main rendering treats σέ as the accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression, “your undertaking to administer,” while the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς refer to the first-person speaker, who knows himself to have received rather than given a favor. An alternative analysis makes τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν the object of ἀναδέξασθαι, with the speaker undertaking the arrangement that Clement administer. A less contextually suitable reading takes σέ as the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν, so that the speaker undertakes to administer Clement. The explicit accusative can defensibly be the embedded subject, and the immediate commission to Clement supports that choice; no emendation is required.

The supplied print places a raised mark before σωτηρίας although no ordinary elision is apparent. The mark does not affect the intelligible phrase ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων σωτηρίας and is treated as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature.

source_issues.source_quote: πλὴν γινώσκετε πάντες πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
source_issues.issue: γινώσκετε can be indicative (“all of you know”) or imperative (“all of you should recognize”). The main text adopts the exhortation because it stands amid directives about supporting the bishop; an appeal to knowledge the hearers already possess remains a defensible alternative. The bishop is expressed by an accusative noun with the agreeing participle κάμνοντα, not by an infinitive.

passages.text: After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and entreated me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from the life here (as is owed to me), you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother, reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, heeding the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city. Then, toward the end, do not hesitate also to disclose the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair. For discourse that leads astray destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: there in the midst before everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the public location in the assembly’s midst and the presence of all as witnesses.
Construes the infinitive with the following finite verb despite the printed period, yielding the natural sense of earnestly urging Clement to take the chair.
Introduces a formal request made before the assembled brothers.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats the resumed σέ as the accusative subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον. English supplies “account” and “it” from the act of writing in epitome because διαπέμπω otherwise lacks an expressed object.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood
lexical_decisions.rationale: Presents the requested record as extending to Clement’s earliest stated thoughts or reflections.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων
lexical_decisions.chosen: the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the unusual coordination in which κηρυχθέντων grammatically characterizes both the words and the deeds.
Πρόφασις can denote cause, occasion, or pretext; an account of Peter’s death supports “cause” here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην
lexical_decisions.chosen: what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the necessary suffering as an obligation that the speaker has paid or fulfilled in a devout manner.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text pairs life-giving words with ἀγνοῶν and the church’s rule with οὐκ εἰδώς. The alternative shared-object/absolute-participle attachment and the printed punctuation are disclosed separately; both source negations remain represented.
Renders πλάνος by its active force of causing hearers to wander or be deceived.

source_issues.issue: The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes them together as “entreated me to sit.” This treats the punctuation as an editorial feature of the supplied edition, not as proof that the Greek words are corrupt.
The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπαρόντων. It is intelligible as the form conventionally normalized συμπαρόντων and does not impede translation.

source_issues.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
source_issues.issue: The main construction takes the second σέ as a resumed accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with Clement and διαπέμψαι denoting his dispatch of the resulting account to James. The following section’s statement that Clement made and sent the epitome supports this role assignment. Alternatively, σέ could formally be taken as the object of διαπέμψαι, “send you,” but that would require the speaker to remain the unexpressed subject and fits the ensuing account less well. The object sent is unexpressed in Greek and is supplied in English from the writing of the epitome.

source_issues.source_quote: ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
source_issues.issue: The main text takes the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς directly with δηλῶσαι: after the earlier request to write and send the account, Clement is specifically told not to hesitate to disclose the cause of the death near its end. It is also possible to give “do not hesitate” wider scope over both the dispatch and the final disclosure. The selected narrower attachment follows the immediate position of δηλῶσαι and yields a defensible sequence of instructions.

source_issues.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
source_issues.issue: The first οὐκ can be read with broad propositional scope: it was not a man characterized as unlearned and ignorant who was entrusted with the chair. This is the main rendering and coheres with James’s resulting consolation. A strictly local reading produces “a not-unlearned man” who nevertheless is ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule, an awkward contrast. Another possible analysis distributes the first negation over the coordinated descriptions, yielding the positive sense that the successor was neither unlearned nor ignorant. The explicit second negation in οὐκ εἰδώς is retained as “not knowing the church’s rule.” The ambiguity concerns scope, not an unreadable source.

The printed period interrupts the sequence of descriptions before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the characterization of the man entrusted with the chair. The punctuation is preserved as a disclosed editorial feature and does not by itself establish corruption or require a conjectural reading.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
source_issues.issue: The main text attaches ζωοποιοὺς λόγους to ἀγνοῶν and ἐκκλησίας κανόνα to οὐκ εἰδώς, preserving the two distinct formulations for ignorance. An alternative groups both objects with ἀγνοῶν and takes οὐκ εἰδώς absolutely (“without knowledge”). The main attachment is more direct despite the printed period; that punctuation and the separate scope of the first negation remain disclosed rather than silently corrected.

editorial_revision.actor: Codex assistant, not human scholarly review

changes.before: Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop toils more than all of you
changes.after: Nevertheless, all of you should recognize that the bishop toils more than all of you

changes.before: ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge
changes.after: ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule

editorial_revision.scope: Correct the participle explanation and disclose the indicative/imperative and object-attachment alternatives; fresh source review required.
